formula: delay_ms = min( index, max_effective ) * step, where max_effective = clamp( max, 1, 50 ) when the max attribute is present

modes.own: block carries its own step; index is its position among matching siblings
modes.children: parent carries the step for the animated blocks inside it; index is the position in page order

stored_sources: eye-care-test (read-only query, 2026-10-13): own step 70 with max 7 on wp_template 438; children step 70 with max 7 on page 208. Canary fixtures hold no stagger values.
default_cap_rule: with no max attribute the position is capped at 7, so delay_ms = min( index, 7 ) * step
step_clamp_rule: the step attribute must be whole digits and is clamped to 0..1000; any other text means no stagger applies (delay_ms null)
max_clamp_rule: the max attribute is clamped to 1..50
dom_rule: each dom row holds a small page as html; the element marked data-case-target is the one whose stagger delay is read; delay_ms is null when no stagger applies

dom_rows.description: Three blocks with their own step sit side by side; the target is the second.
Each block with its own step sits in its own list item; the target is in the third item.
Each block sits three wrappers below the repeating level; the target is in the second repeat.
Each block sits four wrappers below the repeating level, one past the reach; the position falls back to zero.
A lone block with its own step has no matching sibling at any level; the position is zero.
Siblings without a step do not count as peers; the target is the second of two blocks with a step, so its position is one.
A block inside another animated block belongs to that block, not to the staggering parent above it, and has no stagger of its own.
The staggering parent counts the animated blocks that belong to it only: the block after a nested group is third, not fifth.
The group is in page order through plain wrappers; the target is the fourth animated block.
Two staggering parents nest; the block belongs to the nearest one.
A block with its own step ignores its parent step and uses the own-step position.
No step on the block or any parent: no stagger applies.
